scenes.discovery: Line 149 (Rufus on security disclosure requirements for AI companies) is the one new thought in the closing; it arrives without follow-up and disappears.
scenes.repetition: Lines 144-147 re-summarise the story facts already fully explored in Segment 2. The exit sequence (lines 153-160) runs two sign-offs: a warm exit and then a cold listener-question that restarts the energy rather than closing it.

review_before_repairs.rufus_feature: The Wall Street dispatch (lines 76-78) names a real mechanism (land-and-expand, paid-tier pipeline) and stays within sourced facts, correctly flagging no trading data. However it reads as three consecutive Rufus turns with no interruption or studio reaction until Jamie's 'Can I push on something?' at line 79, which arrives after the feature has already ended. The imagined setting ('Picture Wall Street') is established but immediately drops into product-announcement language. The responsive studio exchange exists but is separated from the feature by a full beat, weakening the sense of a live filing returned to the desk.
remaining_issues: Lines 99-101: 'I'd start with a better question' appears in Rufus's mouth (line 99) and then identically in Alex's (line 101); the sponsor re-read mid-Segment 3 exposes a production seam and breaks scene.
Lines 56-57 restate sourcing caveats already covered at lines 15-16 and 48; the close of Segment 2 treads ground rather than landing on new ground.
Rufus's dispatch has no mid-feature studio interruption; Jamie's push comes after the feature closes, reducing the 'responsive exchange' to a delayed reaction.

Segment 5 closing is two sequential exits (lines 153-160): the warm sign-off and then a detached listener-question that re-opens energy at the end; the Rufus observation on security-disclosure regulation (line 149) is the episode's sharpest new idea and receives no follow-up.
Lines 136-138 end the banking scene on mutual agreement rather than honest unresolved tension; the 'some of both' answer at line 133 is accurate but allows the scene to coast out.
